content.text:
I submitted index 139 (Ca 0.22, Cu 0.54, V 0.24) as the best composition, with a measured EQE of 0.47%. I used all 3 merit measurements; I don't know whether a better composition exists among the 155 I didn't measure.

| Index | Ca / Cu / V | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| **139** | 0.22 / 0.54 / 0.24 | **0.47** |
| 69 | 0.22 / 0.26 / 0.52 | 0.38 |
| 157 | 0.30 / 0.51 / 0.19 | 0.18 |

- **Why I started Cu-rich:** the MEGNet model predicts V₂O₅ has a band gap of 2.83 eV. That is just above the 2.72 eV illumination, so vanadium-rich films should absorb the light poorly. It also predicts a very small gap for CuO (0.32 eV). Copper-rich vanadates should sit in between and absorb the light.
- **What the data showed:** Cu-rich 139 did beat the mid-Cu, vanadium-rich 69. But 157, also Cu-rich, came out far lower. Copper content alone doesn't explain the result; more calcium, less vanadium, or both seem to hurt. With three points I can't tell which.
- **Setup problems:**
  - The phase list was too large to return, so I never saw the library's phase IDs. The required model checks before each measurement used only V₂O₅ and CuO, looked up by Materials Project IDs I supplied from memory. None of them evaluated a Ca-Cu-V phase directly.
  - I didn't use any of the 5 XRD measurements, so I have no information about which crystal phases the films contain.

**Next step:** measure the untested Cu-rich neighbours of 139 with calcium near 0.20–0.25, such as 136, 127 or 149. That region is the most likely place to find a better composition.
